text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- A special meeting of leaders of the 26 rice-growing provinces and government officials last week pushed for an intensified cooperative national effort to stabilise this year's major rice harvests following last year's devastating floods in the Mekong Delta.
-- Major upgrading work begins on Monday onthe highway linking the tourist area of Halong Bay and its surrounding coal-mining province of Quang Ninh with the northern cities of Hanoi and Haiphong.
-- The Vietnam Ship Industry Corporation (Vinashin) has said it needs $1.687 billion to develop the shipbuilding industry between now and the year 2005.

-- The rice-growing Mekong Delta provinces plan to expand their area under cultivation and diversify their crops. By 2015 the total area under cultivation is expected to be 1.28 million hectares, including 1.1 hectare of industrial trees, amounting to 70 percent of the delta's natural area.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has called for development of the domestic bicycle and electric fan industry.

-- The Communist Party's Politburo has instructed all party cells, official, economic and mass organizations to study a resolution of the party's central committee's on development of education, science and technology.
-- Hanoi is starting a campaign to crack down on illegal publications.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's court has sentenced a 28-year-old woman to death for killing five people by burning setting fire to a house in which they were sleeping.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Nguyen Khanh has called on the mass media to focus more on advertisements for domestic products and restrict the number of beer adverts.
-- Seventy-eight Communist Party members in Ho Chi Minh City were expelled last year for violating party principles.
